pr_title: Import alternative names in import nmbs flow
pr_body:
## Proposed change
Fixes https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/136896
Alternative solution than the solution proposed in https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/136962

* Create an repair issue for every station not found. (Instead of just the last invalid station name)
* Allow importing when a localized station name is used (dutch, french, germany or english) - now it's just English and the standard names

Should be cherry-picked to beta if possible.

pr_comments:
The 'problem' with this approach is it still requires an exact match while in the past everything was allowed.

The iRail api itself does not care about a hyphen or capital letter, it doesn't even need to be a full match (e.g. Brussel Noord, mol, Berchem... would just work; Brussel gets matched with the first one, central...).

So while it would've just worked before migration, even though it was technically an invalid configuration, it wouldn't work anymore after this and just get a repair.

I've taken a further look into this and while what you're explaining is technically true, the documentation of the integration mentions the following: 

The stations can only be provided by their standard names and not ids. The list of stations can be checked on the NMBS/SNCB website but for most accurate results check them on the [iRail API page](https://api.irail.be/stations/) which this integration uses internally.

If we follow the documentation to the letter we should not even import the alternative/localised names. However, I already discussed this with @joostlek and his response was (paraphrased and translated from Dutch):
> Well, the thing is, it has worked for everyone so far. So, is it a user error? Technically, yes, but that’s not the kind of response they’d appreciate. And since we’ve already put quite some effort into importing it, we should make sure we do it properly so that effort doesn’t go to waste.
Should I conclude out of that, that we're not going to merge either of one?

I believe the API call as in #136962 would catch more 'misconfigurations'. It might take some extra calls if users have a long list with multiple not-exactly-matching names, but should be limited. Also, this would only happen during a migration from yaml. Setting up from the UI requires a user to select stations from a predefined list. Once the import is removed (HA version 2025.7.0) we can also remove the extra lookup. The adjusted repair is of course a good addition.

issue_context.title: several stations not imported in migration to NMBS config flow
issue_context.body: ### The problem as reported in the #beta for 2025.2, after updating and importing a repair is raised for Brussel-Noord while below yaml has been working for years just fine. also, the connections with Utrecht Centraal are not imported either, but they dont show a repair. ### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue? 2025.2.1 ### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core? 2025.1.x ### What type of installation are you running? Home Assistant OS ### Integration causing the issue NMBS ### Link to integration documentation on our website https://rc.home-assistant.io/integrations/nmbs/ ### Diagnostics information _No response_ ### Example YAML snippet ```yaml # Brussel-Noord/Bruxelles-Nord - platform: nmbs station_from: Essen station_to: Brussel-Noord station_live: 'Essen' exclude_vias: true name: Essen - Brussel Noord show_on_map: true - platform: nmbs station_from: Brussel-Noord station_to: Essen station_live: 'Brussel-Noord' exclude_vias: true name: Brussel Noord - Essen show_on_map: true - platform: nmbs station_from: Brussel-Noord station_to: Utrecht Centraal station_live: 'Utrecht Centraal' exclude_vias: true name: Brussel Noord - Utrecht Centraal show_on_map: true ``` ### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us? ```txt ``` ### Additional information
comments:
[nmbs documentation](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/nmbs)
[nmbs source](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/tree/dev/homeassistant/components/nmbs)
Cc @silamon @tjorim

So we check the old name against a list of stations from the API.

From the old docs:
> The stations can only be provided by their standard names and not ids. The list of stations can be checked on the NMBS/SNCB website but for most accurate results check them on the [iRail API page](https://api.irail.be/stations/) which this integration uses internally.

The list with stations has this for Brussel-Noord:
`<station URI="http://irail.be/stations/NMBS/008812005" id="BE.NMBS.008812005" locationX="4.360846" locationY="50.859663" standardname="Brussel-Noord/Bruxelles-Nord">Brussels-North</station>`

So technically a user should have used `Brussel-Noord/Bruxelles-Nord`.
From one of their Git repos:
> (standard)name: the most neutral name of the station (e.g., in Wallonia use the French name, for Brussels use both, for Flanders use nl name)

Some observations at first glance:
The previous version did not validate the station name, the irail API we rely on just tried to figure it out.
Now we actually check if the name matches the standard name or name (which is usually gonna be English because how we set up and use the pyrail library), so in fact we are already more forgiving than before.
For me it's clear this could be described as a user error (but we allowed it before) and not something we should fix.
We could have a grace period where we check for more, but we would (need to) split up the `standardname` by `/` and I'm not sure if that will even catch all cases.
But is it possible to request to the api with the old value and then get the station we used to get?

> But is it possible to request to the api with the old value and then get the station we used to get?

We could, but we don't know if a user used the Dutch or French name.
By default, we always request English which will be the name. The standardname depends on the location of the station: the French name in Wallonia, the Dutch name in Flanders, a combo of both for Brussels.
I mean, we now store them with the identifier right? So I don't mind what name they used, as long as we can find the right station for that name, we can just import it
In theory the irail API would have even figured out the German name if a user used it. But we never get that in the data from the API (unless we set the language to German in our iRail constructor).
Is there an API endpoint we can use to get the station by name?

> Is there an API endpoint we can use to get the station by name?

No there does not seem to be one.

I'm not sure if we rely on the station name or ID now.
It looks like the unique id is based on the name (easy for a user to see and recognize) but we can't be certain a station never changes name. I think it's better to rely on the station id (just some random numbers). Example from 2022-2023: Charleroi-Sud/Charleroi-Zuid changed their name to Charleroi-Central/Charleroi-Centraal (and Louvain in 2017, Liège in 2018).

```py
        return [
            SelectOptionDict(value=station["id"], label=station["standardname"])
            for station in self.stations
        ]
```

So yes, we now create the entries unique id based on the identifier of the station.

So the thing I would be looking for here, is there a way to get to the identifier of the station using the old name? Is the id present in the route info?

We're using the identifier of the station right now, but import allowed any name (dutch, french, german, english). There's also a combined name that coudl be used in import based on where the station is located (brussels = dutch/french, flanders = dutch, ...)
It's fixable, but we need to fetch the stations for every language if import is given. 

While multiple repair issues are added, the key is the same, so if multiple stations are valid, only the last one is kept.
Then I guess the easiest way to do it is partial search (nl/fr are divided by a /) in the async_step_import which should cover most cases.

So looking at https://github.com/tjorim/pyrail/blob/main/examples/connections.json, the station info of both the arrival and departure station is provided in a connections call. So why don't we modify the yaml import to do a connections request with the old config, and then extract the identifiers and use them.

Does that make sense? We would only have to check what happens if the station does not exist
We need to fetch the alternative names from the stations api, since the connections api doesn't guarantee to return connections (for example around midnight)

> We need to fetch the alternative names from the stations api, since the connections api doesn't guarantee to return connections (for example around midnight)

I wanted to say to check the liveboard endpoint instead but that also doesn't always return trains at times like midnight. Could we not set a fixed time in the future where there should definitely be some connections? E.g. 10h the next day?

Edit: while there are no trains (departures) in the liveboard all the time, I still expect it to contain the station information. Since right now there are still trains everywhere I can't check this.

thanks for the quick action.
please also see why Utrecht Centraal is not imported.
as far as I can tell this is the exact name I used from https://api.irail.be/stations/ and this time there is no Dutch/French issue

`<station URI="http://irail.be/stations/NMBS/008400621" id="BE.NMBS.008400621" locationX="5.109722" locationY="52.089167" standardname="Utrecht Centraal">Utrecht Centraal</station>`

wait, would it be because of the route from Brussel-Noord, which is causing the trouble. let me try a different connection 

```
  - platform: nmbs
    station_from: Roosendaal
    station_to: Utrecht Centraal
    station_live: 'Utrecht Centraal'
    exclude_vias: true
    name: Roosendaal - Utrecht Centraal
    show_on_map: true
```

__update__
yes that seems to fix Utrecht Centraal.

would this be the place to ask for the reason behind the breaking name change of the live boards? Changing to 'Trains in x' seems to not cover the full info here, and breaks frontend unnecessarily.

added to that, as we noticed yesterday, during night times, there are no trains for many of these connections, which breaks functionality completely, returning unknown for these entities

Id be happy to open a separate issue for this, but as @tjorim already mentioned it in https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/136896#issuecomment-2624126992 here we might keep that functionality issue here too?

I don't know the details or exact reasoning but this was discussed in https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/121548. I never used this integration before so I'm not sure about prior behaviour. When I think of liveboard or connections, I imagine a setup with actions to get a list of planned trains (like weather integrations with their get forecast action). I'm not sure if it's ideal to have a sensor per connection, a bunch of attributes... This almost feels like something that needs a general architecture discussion.

I have to mention that I was the one driving the change to avoid implementing the live board separately. The downside of the live board implementation is a lot of attributes in the entity. Ideally that can be replaced by just an action that returns the data which can be used to automate with

ok I see. but, given the fact the new entities are identical to the former 'live' entities, showing the same and the same number of attributes (which I kind of like tbh, I really dont hope these will be scattered to even more single out entities....) changing only their entity_id and name is breaking, and unnecessary? just trying to avoid users to all see this: while the migration could have prevented that by using the same naming scheme
You're saying the unique id got changed?

sorry I didnt check the unique_id, only the name and entity_id... but being able to still edit that in the UI indicates the unique_id of this entity wasn't changed, it is simply no longer available, and the new entities get new unique_id's. also, I can confirm that changing the yaml config to ``` - platform: nmbs station_from: Essen station_to: Brussel-Noord/Bruxelles-Nord # <--- use full multi language station identifier station_live: 'Essen' exclude_vias: true name: Essen - Brussel Noord show_on_map: true - platform: nmbs station_from: Brussel-Noord/Bruxelles-Nord # <--- station_to: Essen station_live: 'Brussel-Noord/Bruxelles-Nord' # <--- exclude_vias: true name: Brussel Noord - Essen show_on_map: true ``` now imports the connections correctly. **Might be worth a special mention in the breaking changes**

final note if I may here: all things considered, this is not very productive: why not have the user confirm creating the 'Trains in x' entity per configuration entry, as the 'station_live' from the yaml did. seems waste of resource even though disabled, and confusing (are they really identical....?) the rest is working ok now feel free to close if nothing more to add or fix
I'm going to fix whatever is fixable, but I'm still unsure what to do with the liveboard feature. Thank you for testing, that's very much appreciated!

I'll be opening a PR that does the following things: 
* Create an repair issue for every station not found. (Instead of just the last invalid station name)
* Allow importing when a localized station name is used (dutch, french, germany or english) - now it's just English and the standard names

I'm a bit lost to what should be done with the liveboards. There were separate config flows at the very start when I developed this, but during reviews phase these were abandoned and combined together, so setting up the connection from and to station would give a liveboard for from and to station as disabled.

Struggling to set up a dev instance of HA to test my changes but I think #136962 should tackle at least part of the problem.
Edit: I think I'm looking in the wrong place so will close the PR for now.
Edit2: managed to fix it, importing works, an actual fake station will still throw the up the repair.

review_comments: Now includes the invalid station name, so multiple issues are given if multiple station names are invalid.
